title: \(\mathrm{P}_{R}\) versus \(\mathrm{NP}_{R}\) in the Blum–Shub–Smale model
formal: Is \(\mathrm{P}_{\mathbb{R}}=\mathrm{NP}_{\mathbb{R}}\) for the unit-cost Blum–Shub–Smale model over the ordered field of real numbers?
definitions: Inputs are finite tuples \(x\in \mathbb{R} ^{n}\), with input size n. A machine has a finite program and finitely many fixed real constants. It can store and copy real numbers, perform +, −, ×, and division by a nonzero number, and branch on the sign or equality to zero of a stored real, at unit cost per operation; the ordinary BSS input, output and register-shift operations are included. \(\mathrm{P}_{\mathbb{R}}\) consists of subsets of the disjoint union of the spaces \(\mathbb{R} ^{n}\) decidable by one such deterministic machine in polynomially many steps as a function of n. \(\mathrm{NP}_{\mathbb{R}}\) consists of sets for which membership of x is equivalent to existence of a real witness y of length bounded by a polynomial in n that is accepted by one deterministic BSS verifier in polynomially many steps. Machine constants are finite and independent of input length; witnesses may contain arbitrary reals. The target is equality of these classes, not equality in a finite-precision or bit-cost model.

context_blocks.text: The BSS model treats exact field operations and order tests as elementary computation. Its version of nondeterminism allows real witnesses and captures basic real algebraic feasibility problems.

This separation is a foundational question about algebraic computation over a continuum. Classical P versus NP does not by itself answer it: the input representation, cost model and certificates differ.

The recommended paper studies Boolean inputs to real computation. Proposition 1.1 identifies \(\mathrm{BP}(\mathrm{P}_{\mathbb R}^{0})=\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{PosSLP}}\), where the superscript 0 permits only machine constants 0 and 1. PosSLP asks whether an arithmetic straight-line program using 0, 1, addition, subtraction and multiplication outputs a positive integer. Theorem 1.4 places PosSLP in the counting hierarchy.

With arbitrary fixed real constants, \(\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{PosSLP}}/\mathrm{poly}=\mathrm{BP}(\mathrm{P}_{\mathbb R})\) is Conjecture 1.2 in that paper. These Boolean-input results do not settle equality of deterministic and nondeterministic BSS classes on arbitrary real inputs.

why: The defining complexity-class question for exact computation over the reals, connecting TCS to algebraic geometry and numerical computation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, preserving the quantifiers, model and guarantees. Conditional results settle only their conditional claims. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
